32:_: (132) And all this in a place, etc. — this "and all this" refers to where we qualified by placing a lechi in the middle of the mavo when they did not make a lechi at the head of the mavo; and it says that this is specifically when in this half of the mavo alone there is also mavo name, that it has all the conditions required for this [as Shulchan Aruch concludes and as written above in siman 366]; if not so, it has courtyard law and requires a mashehu pas, etc., as above in seif 2; and Shulchan Aruch does not refer to if they also made lechi outside and joined together, for for this one need not have all the details in that half of the mavo, for the entire mavo joins together for this [Peri Megadim]; and see there what he wrote further on this:
33:א: (133) That it is twenty amot wide — and it deals with when he does not wish to make tzurat hapetach at the mavo opening, for this helps even however wide the mavo is, as at the end of siman 366:
33:ב: (134) Four amot wide — and in less than this it does not help, even though each side is less than ten, for the air of this side and that side comes and nullifies it; unlike when he makes it four amot wide as the measure along a mavo wall, as in siman 366 — air from here and there cannot nullify it, for air cannot nullify a mavo wall. And what is written "and he places it in the middle" means along the length of the mavo:
33:ג: (135) Since its length, etc. — and it is also required that the pas not be low less than ten tefachim, as the law of a mavo wall, as in siman 366:
33:ד: (136) At its head — meaning that it reaches from one mavo wall to the wall opposite it, to permit both sides; and the same, he can correct them by lechayim — lechi from here and lechi from here, or lechi on one and korah on one [meaning one head on the mavo wall and its other head on the pas], like other mavo'ot:
33:ה: (137) Placed on the pas, etc. — to exclude if the pas is low, even though the korah touches from this wall to the opposite wall, it does not help, for behold through the pas it is considered as two mavo'ot, for it is considered as a wall, and if so each mavo's korah is placed only on one wall:
33:ו: (138) Or within, etc. — for it is as lavud:
33:ז: (139) And every condition of a mavo — as explained above in siman 366; if not so, its law is like a courtyard, and korah does not help in it, but only two lechayim of mashehu on its two sides, as explained above in seif 2:
33:ח: (140) And what is from the pas, etc. — meaning, besides the korah correction made at the mavo opening, one must make another correction at the end of the pas length, as the law of a crooked mavo explained in siman 364 end of seif 3, even if there are not ten amot from the end of the pas length to the middle wall:
33:ט: (141) Bent in the middle and open — should read: bent in the middle and open:
33:י: (142) At their two heads to reshus ha-rabbim — and therefore one must make tzurat hapetach at the end of the pas length to the middle wall opposite it, and it is like one who made a pas along the entire mavo length:
33:כ: (143) For it does not have crooked mavo law, etc. — for although it is explained below in siman 364 regarding a crooked mavo made like a chet, that even if from the beginning of the bend to the middle wall is not ten amot, correction is still required there — there it is different, for it is actually crooked; but here one can say that through the pas they become as two mavo'ot completely divided to their ends; and although the pas does not reach the middle wall, nevertheless since from the end of the pas to the opposite wall is not more than ten amot, it is considered an opening and is like two mavo'ot completely divided, only that there is an opening from one to the other; unlike when more than ten amot, one cannot say it is like an opening, and therefore its law is like a crooked mavo; and for practical law Acharonim agreed the main view is like the first reasoning; and see Biur Halacha:
33:ל: (144) More than ten amot — as it should read:
34:א: (145) And he makes a pas three amot wide — for thereby standing becomes greater than the breach at its side and it is considered closed; and although generally we hold that breach like standing is also permitted, as explained in siman 362 seif 9 — here it is different, for it is also breached from the other side, and in such a case where they are equal we say the air of this side and that side comes and nullifies it:
34:ב: (146) And an opening ten amot wide remains — and nevertheless lechi or korah is required to permit the mavo, for it is not better than other ordinary mavo'ot; and one places the korah only on the area of ten amot [and likewise when making lechi, he places it at the head of the ten amot], for from the pasin onward until the walls it is permitted otherwise because of standing greater than breach:
34:ג: (147) And likewise every similar case — meaning that he distances four amot from the wall and makes a pas of six amot [Rashi]:
34:ד: (148) And one must beware, etc. — but from the default we are not concerned lest they walk through the small one and leave the large one, for the presumption is that a person does not leave a large opening and enter through a small one:
34:ה: (149) That if he did so, etc. — meaning that thereby the opening status of the large one is nullified, and the lechi or korah corrected in it is nullified, and this mavo is found without correction:
34:ו: (150) For the small one — see Chiddushei R' Akiva Eiger who wonders what helps in making tzurat hapetach for the small one after opening status was nullified from the large one; and the correct view is as written in Sefer Tiferet Shmuel that it is a scribal error and should read "for the large one," and now it is well explained that after tzurat hapetach was made, opening status was not nullified from it even if they do not walk through it:
35:_: (151) When complete it is considered — meaning, and therefore it is not relevant to say in this the air of this side and that side comes and nullifies it:
36:א: (152) And a slope to reshus ha-rabbim — where the mavo ground was higher than reshus ha-rabbim ground and he had to slope at its opening toward reshus ha-rabbim:
36:ב: (153) Or level to reshus ha-rabbim, etc. — where reshus ha-rabbim was higher than mavo ground, and the mavo entry also from the opening inward was high like reshus ha-rabbim ground for the width of an amah or half an amah, and afterward it became a slope toward the middle side:
36:ג: (154) That raises ten, etc. — meaning that if the slope is four amot long, then the ground is already raised above ten tefachim and is like a partition; but if ten collect within five amot, it is as if it does not exist and is like other ground whose use is pleasant for walking:
36:ד: (155) And it requires no correction — for that height at the side of the opening is a partition, even though it slopes and continues; and this is what Rama concludes, "and with this mound," etc.:
36:ה: (156) And with this mound, etc. — and if the entire city is surrounded by a mound and afterward they built houses in it, it is forbidden, for it is not enclosed for dwelling, as written siman 358 seif 2; and see there seif 8, that even if he built partitions ten high on the mound it does not help; and if the mound was less than ten tefachim and he completed to ten tefachim, it helps, for this enclosure is enclosure for dwelling made after the city was built. Therefore one can correct even if the mound was around the entire city — meaning he diminishes from the mound in an area more than ten amot wide until it is not ten tefachim high, for then it is considered a breach, and afterward he completes this measure, and through this it helps, as above in siman 358 seif 2 see there:
36:ו: (157) Like a partition — and if around the city there is a ditch ten tefachim deep and four tefachim wide, which is like a partition, and the ditch was closed with earth and stones — if the closing does not rise more than ten amot, behold it is like an opening and does not forbid; but if it is more than ten amot, behold it is like a breach:
